label: Стенка
description: A 10-sentence usage card for стенка (wall unit).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Стенка' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'стоит'. 'Эта' is the agreeing feminine demonstrative, and 'в гостиной' is a prepositional location phrase.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Стенку' is the accusative direct object of 'купили', and 'новую' is the agreeing feminine accusative adjective. The first-declension ending -а shifts to -у.

missions.phrase: У нас нет места для стенки.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Genitive after для. The preposition 'для' requires the genitive 'стенки'. The phrase also contains the genitive of absence 'нет места', a doubly useful pattern.

missions.phrase: Я подошёл к стенке с книгами.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Dative after к. The preposition 'к' governs the dative, giving 'стенке'. 'С книгами' adds an instrumental phrase describing what the unit holds.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after со. The preposition 'рядом со' requires the instrumental 'стенкой'. This is a natural way to describe furniture placement in a room.

missions.phrase: В стенке много полок и ящиков.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Prepositional case. After 'в' the noun takes the prepositional form 'стенке'. 'Много полок и ящиков' adds two genitive-plural nouns describing the contents.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Стенки' is the nominative plural, the subject of the sentence. 'Эти' and 'дорогие' are the agreeing plural demonstrative and adjective.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural object. 'Стенки' is the accusative plural object of 'продают'; this inanimate feminine plural matches the nominative form. 'Красивые' agrees in the plural.
Strategic focus: Genitive of possession. 'Стенки' is the genitive showing whose shelves these are. 'На полках' is a prepositional-plural location phrase nested inside the description.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject with accusative object. 'Стенка' is the nominative subject of 'занимает', while 'целую стену' is its accusative object, contrasting the unit with the actual wall.
